item.title: Controlling JUnit Test Execution Order: Methods and Alternatives
item.description:
“Controlling JUnit Test Execution Order: Methods and Alternatives”

A frequently encountered requirement in testing, particularly with integration or workflow-driven scenarios, is dictating the precise order in which test methods execute. The core philosophy behind JUnit, as stated in its own FAQ, is that test method invocation order is not guaranteed, promoting independence between tests. However, when tests inherently represent sequential steps (e.g., setup, action, verification), this arbitrariness can cause issues.

item.title: Java Unit Testing Strategies for Capturing System Out and Error Streams
item.description:
“Java Unit Testing Strategies for Capturing System Out and Error Streams”

When crafting unit tests for Java code that writes directly to the console via System.out or System.err, standard assertion mechanisms fall short. We require specific techniques to redirect this output stream temporarily to an in-memory buffer, enabling verification of the written content. How can we reliably capture and assert standard output and error streams during testing? Several effective strategies exist, ranging from manual stream manipulation to leveraging dedicated testing libraries.
